title: Nano Banana Pro Unexpected Event Photo Prompt
description: A detailed prompt for nano-banana-pro (referred to as 'banana pro' in the tweet) that transforms a static portrait into a realistic snapshot of an unexpected event occurring. It instructs the model to maintain identity while adding dynamic reactions and physical interactions with a customizable surprise element.
promptText:
[Unexpected Event Requirement]
{argument name="event" default="Fill in a sudden event here, e.g., 'a bird suddenly flies past the camera', 'a tiger appears from behind the subject', etc. If left blank, the model will design a reasonable sudden event based on the original scene."}
Maintain the identity, appearance, hairstyle, clothing, environment, scene structure, and overall visual style consistent with the original image.
Reconstruct the ordinary static photo into a **realistic snapshot capturing the '0.1 second after a sudden event occurs'**.
1 | The unexpected event must actually happen
Strictly execute the event defined in [Unexpected Event Requirement].
The event must exist realistically in the final image; it cannot be implied solely through facial expressions or body language.
The position, size, direction of movement, and perspective relationships of the event must comply with real photography logic and have natural spatial relationships with the original environment.
If the event involves motion, clearly express the direction and sense of speed.
The event can be located in:
Foreground of the lens
Near the subject
To the side of the subject
Behind the subject
Background area
Crossing between the subject and the lens
Choose the most visually impactful position freely based on the nature of the event.

2 | The subject must react instinctively to the event
The subject is not posing but making a real, unprepared instinctive reaction at the moment the event occurs.
Automatically design movements compliant with human biomechanics based on the event's position, speed, danger level, and direction of movement, such as:
Sudden lateral evasion, leaning back, leaning forward, turning around, crouching low, jumping away, losing balance, emergency stop, striding to dodge, reaching out to block, arms protecting the body, grabbing nearby objects to maintain balance, etc.
Do not limit actions to just "dodging backward."
Redesign the direction of the subject's body reaction based on the position and trajectory of the sudden event.

3 | Actions must have a complete kinetic chain
The subject's movement must form a complete dynamic transfer from feet → legs → hips → torso → shoulders → arms → head.
Clearly show:
Shift in center of gravity
Difference between supporting leg and moving leg
Counter-rotation of hips and shoulders
Head quickly turning toward the event
Arms performing protective, blocking, grabbing, or balancing actions
Natural inertial movement of clothes, hair, and body
Avoid static poses like standing straight with feet together and hands casually placed, like a model.

4 | Facial expressions must causally relate to the event
The expression must be the immediate reaction after seeing the sudden event.
Automatically match emotions based on the event:
Surprise, shock, alertness, fear, confusion, helpless laughter, astonishment, instinctive dodging, sudden realization of danger, being startled, etc.
Do not deliberately make exaggerated comedic expressions.
The focus is to capture the moment of "What just came?!"

5 | Clear spatial relationship between event and subject
Enhance the spatial depth of foreground, midground, and background.
If the event passes by the subject, let it enter the foreground to create obvious occlusion, motion trails, and visual impact.
If the event appears from behind the subject, ensure the subject's head, shoulders, or body are turning towards it.
If the event enters rapidly from the side, shift the subject's center of gravity in the opposite direction for an immediate dodge.
If the event is large in volume, adjust the scale between the subject and the event according to perspective relationships.
The reason for the subject's movement must be directly visible from the image.

6 | Event takes priority over subject action
The final image is not:
"A person performing a dodge action."
But rather:
"A real event is happening, and the camera captures the subject's immediate reaction to it."
The event itself must become the secondary visual center of the frame.
There must be clear causal, directional, and spatial relationships between the subject's actions and the event.

7 | Photographic effects
Realistic photography, high shutter speed, instant snapshot.
Preserve natural inertial movement but avoid severe motion blur.
The image should possess:
Strong sense of immediacy + spatial depth + dynamic direction + foreground/background relationship + unpredictability.
Both the subject and the event must comply with real-world lighting, shadows, perspective, scale, occlusion, and laws of motion.
The final effect should look like a photographer happened to press the shutter to capture a previously unpredictable moment.
No static posing, no studio feel, no theatrical feel, no deliberately manufactured disasters.
Core goal: Viewers should first see "what happened," and only then notice "how the subject dodged."

title: Intricate Poetic Dragon Fantasy Text
description: An intricate artistic abstract poem describing a timeless dragon with cinematic spatial/temporal elements used for generation testing.
promptText:
Where the Wing Remembers Both Shores

The dragon does not choose a century.
It is the century choosing itself
through a body made of postponement and afterglow.
One wing trails the last unburned page of a library
that fell before paper learned its own name.
The other combs holographic rain
from towers that have not yet decided
whether they will stand or become rumor.
Between them the air keeps two calendars
and forgets which one is running.
Its scales are older than the word for scale.
They remember the heat of forges
that have not been lit,
and the cold of stars
that have already gone out
in some other telling.
Runes surface and sink like thoughts
a city has not earned the right to think.
Each pulse of light is both relic and prototype.
Below, the streets are wet with what has happened
and what is still negotiating its arrival.
Neon writes on water that was once a glacier’s patience
and will be, later, only a rumor of thirst.
Foundations rest on the quiet of forests
that still dream they are standing.
Billboards advertise tomorrows
already homesick for the dusk that has not come.
The creature’s eyes hold the only honest weather:
one the green of a memory
that does not yet know it is finished,
the other the blue of a question
that has not found the mouth that will ask it.
They look at us the way time looks at itself
when no one is watching
without pity, without verdict,
only the long courtesy of attention.
We live in the brief downdraft of its passing,
that strange, merciful interval
where the past is still unfinished with us
and the future has already begun
to miss what we have not yet lost.
Nothing is promised except the turning:	he slow, luminous hinge of a wing
that belongs to every hour at once
and to none of them completely.
The mist it leaves is neither ending nor beginning.
It is the place they briefly recognize each other
before the next uncertainty
opens its quiet, necessary hand.

title: Engraved Digital Painting Style
description: A complex prompt that blends semi-realistic digital painting with traditional engraving techniques, creating a unique texture with warm cinematic lighting.
promptText: Soft {argument name="painting style" default="semi-realistic digital painting"} blended with highly detailed engraving illustration style, combining painterly softness with ultra-fine crosshatching and dotting techniques. Cinematic warm lighting with a strong golden-orange glow illuminating one side of the subject, contrasted by soft cool shadows, enhanced by dramatic chiaroscuro. Skin and textures are rendered through a fusion of smooth luminous digital shading and dense layered engraving lines, creating a balance between soft gradients and intricate linework. Subtle glossy highlights and reflective surfaces are preserved, especially in the eyes, giving a luminous and lifelike appearance. Delicate painterly blending remains visible through soft brush strokes, seamlessly integrated with precise contour lines and micro-detail etching, forming rich textures built from thousands of fine strokes. Edges transition naturally—sharp and clean in focal areas while dissolving into loose sketch-like strokes in unfinished regions. The top of the head and lower body fade into an incomplete sketch effect with soft, disappearing lines and partially dissolved forms blending into the background. Background uses a {argument name="background material" default="textured brown cardboard"} surface with visible matte grain and slightly rough tactile quality, subtly merged with a dark, studio-like atmospheric depth. The composition is minimalistic and elegant, with a calm yet dramatic mood. Color grading leans toward warm, natural tones with a slightly muted and faded palette, maintaining harmony between digital painting warmth and classic engraving aesthetics. High contrast lighting with deep blacks and controlled highlights enhances depth, while maintaining soft transitions in key areas. Ultra-high detail, macro texture emphasis, cinematic shadow depth, museum-quality finish, handcrafted engraving feel, 8K resolution. Ar 9:16!

title: Streetwear Editorial Portrait Identity Retention
description: A high-detail prompt designed to generate a luxury streetwear campaign portrait while maintaining the user's specific facial features and identity.
promptText: Create a cinematic, ultra-realistic streetwear editorial portrait of me, preserving my exact facial identity, features, skin tone, hairstyle, and natural proportions. Style me in {argument name="outfit" default="premium modern streetwear with an oversized layered outfit, subtle accessories"}, and a confident relaxed pose in an {argument name="urban setting" default="urban setting with concrete architecture, textured walls, and understated city details"}. Use {argument name="lighting" default="dramatic natural lighting, soft shadows, shallow depth of field, realistic skin texture, sophisticated neutral tones, subtle film grain"}, high-fashion magazine composition, professional photography, and cinematic color grading. Make the image feel authentic, effortlessly cool, minimal, aesthetic, and editorial, like a luxury streetwear campaign photographed on a full-frame camera with an 85mm lens. I've attached my image here.
